column1: # The package set, and the single source of truth for it.
# build/BuildNugets.sh packs in this order, the CI workflows and the e2e scripts read it, and
# tests/OpenTok.Net.UnitTests asserts it stays consistent with what is actually under src/. Adding a
# package means adding a row here and a project under src/ — nothing else keeps a second copy of the
# list.
# Rows are in dependency order, and BuildNugets.sh relies on it: OpenTok.Net.Maui carries a
# PackageReference on OpenTok.Net and restores it from the local-artifacts feed (see NuGet.config),
# so the core package has to be packed *and merged* before the MAUI one is packed at all.
# Neither row is a native binding. OpenTok.Net.iOS and OpenTok.Net.Android — the packages that
# actually wrap OpenTok.xcframework and opentok-android-sdk.aar — are built and published from
# their own repositories and consumed here as pinned NuGet dependencies (see
# OpenTokIosPackageVersion / OpenTokAndroidPackageVersion in Directory.Build.props), not packed by
# this script.
# Columns
#   id      the NuGet package id, which is also the directory under src/ and the .csproj name
#   heads   which target-framework family the package ships:
#             mobile - both android and ios heads
#   deps    other ids in this repository it depends on, comma separated, or -
# id
OpenTok.Net
OpenTok.Net.Maui
